The government-to-government channel for selling U.S. defense articles, services, and training. The Defense Department sells from its own stocks (Sec. 21) or buys from industry on the purchaser's behalf (Sec. 22), and the purchaser pays the full cost, normally in advance, so the articles themselves need no appropriation.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 82 Stat. 1323](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/82/1323){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 22 U.S.C. 2761-2762](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/2761?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Sec. 21(a): sales from Defense Department stocks at actual value or replacement cost; services at full cost.
- Sec. 21(c): U.S. personnel performing services under a sale may not perform duties of a combatant nature, with reporting to Congress if hostilities endanger them.
- Sec. 21(e): purchasers pay charges that recover the administrative costs of the program.
- Sec. 22(a): procurement for a purchaser on its dependable undertaking to pay the full contract cost.
- Major sales above dollar thresholds require notice to Congress under Sec. 36(b) of the Arms Export Control Act, and a joint resolution can block them.

## Why it matters

FMS is how most major U.S. weapons reach foreign governments, and grant money from [Foreign Military Financing](fmf.qmd) is usually spent through it. Because the State Department approves each case and the Defense Department executes it, oversight runs through the [Arms Export Control Act](aeca-1976.qmd) notification process rather than through appropriations.

## Current status

In force. Enacted in the Foreign Military Sales Act of 1968, which was renamed the Arms Export Control Act in 1976.

[Last checked November 24, 2026.]{.checked}

## Funding and administration

- **Account.** Foreign Military Sales Trust Fund, paid by purchasers rather than appropriations.
- **Run by.** The Defense Security Cooperation Agency and the military departments, with the State Department approving each sale.
- **Committees.** House Foreign Affairs and Senate Foreign Relations, which receive sales notifications under Sec. 36(b).

## Where it sits
